title: Make a scale read 300 grams by choosing the right weights
instruction: make the scale read 300 grams using the weights
context: Measuring out a quantity from standard weights is basic to cooking, pharmacy and lab work. The robot has to read the labels and pick a combination that adds up, and only weights resting on the pan count, so pressing on it or holding a weight over it scores nothing.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Scale pan: a steel disc 18 cm across standing 2 cm tall, fixed, centred 29 cm forward on the midline. (2) Weights: brass cylinders, loose, standing 15 cm forward: 500 g (6.5 cm across, 7 cm tall) 22 cm left; 100 g (5 cm across, 5 cm tall) 10 cm left; two of 200 g (5.5 cm across, 6 cm tall) 10 cm and 22 cm right. (3) Labels: a white card in front of each weight, 6.5 cm nearer the arms, printed "500 G", "100 G", "200 G" and "200 G" in black block characters 1.5 x 2.1 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored once, after the episode ends. The scale reads the total mass of the weights resting still on the pan (centre over the pan, underside within 8 cm of its top, so a weight stacked on another counts). 1.0 for exactly 300 g; 0.5 for 200 g or 400 g; 0.0 for any other reading, including the empty pan.
reset_notes: Put the four weights back on their marks in front of their labels. The pan and labels are fixed (putty) and stay in place.
fidelity: Dream Labs' YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim). The pan is a fixed disc: there is no display, and the reading is computed from the weights resting on it. The weights are rigid cylinders of the stated masses; the label characters are thin black boxes on white cards.
